Changelog

Build 18 (2026-11-11)

  • The logo: the name drawn on a single grid — "lilliput" from bare strokes, squares and 2 arcs, every stroke 1 gap from the next, so the word reads as a pulse train; its icon, "li". In assets/logo (SVG: the logotype in white, in black and with the channels' colours; the icon), made by tools/gen_logo.py. The splash draws it 1 unit to a pixel, the build under it; the README opens with it.

Build 17 (2026-11-11)

  • A new RHYTHM for the mixer no longer restarts the drums (it did, audibly). A single beat clock runs both: whichever starts, or gets a new pattern, comes in on the next beat; the other plays on untouched.
  • The drums' rhythms anew, after the genre (Bigorna's generator; Attack Magazine's industrial and dark Berlin techno breakdowns; the genre's descriptions): POWER 4/4, PISTON, MARCH, OFFBEAT, RUMBLE, BROKEN, 3 AGAINST 4, TRIBAL, SHUFFLE, DIST BREAK, HALF RITUAL, BURST FILL. Every lane in 16ths, 16 or 32 steps: the pace is always the tempo's (before, kicks on every 16th read as double time, and 7-, 9- and 10-step lanes or a hat at 1/8 lost the pace). Swing only where the genre swings.
  • A 4th voice, PERC: struck metal (ANVIL, PIPE, SHEET, CLANK, CHAIN, SPRING, GRIND), white key 4 on the drums' pages.
  • A voice's white key held 0.7 s mutes it (its key blinks, dim; its page says MUTED); held again, back.
  • The drums' own LEVEL is gone from their 3rd page: a voice's LEVEL is the only one.
  • COMPRESSOR, SEQ's first page: on the mixer's sound, before the drums; AMOUNT compresses, brings the mix forward and, with SIDECHAIN on KICK, ducks it under each kick (up to 18 dB) — more AMOUNT, more lift and more pump. THRESH, RELEASE; with SHIFT, ATTACK and RATIO. Sessions keep it.
  • Sessions saved with build 16's drums load with PERC resting.
  • The sine table moved from the RAM for code to the RAM's pool (2 KiB of code room back); the sound is the same, bit for bit.

Build 16 (2026-11-10)

  • DRUMS: a drum section beside the mixer, after Ruismaker Noir (Bram Bos): KICK, SNARE and HATS, a single engine (a swept tone and filtered noise, ATTACK from a hard transient to 100 ms, DECAY, CLICK, METAL, DRIVE), each with its lane of steps (accents, pitches, ALT) on the RHYTHM's tempo, coming in on its beat. Black key 9 (3rd from the right): short, their pages; SHIFT +, a new drum rhythm; held, on or off. On their pages white keys 1-3 choose the voice (SHIFT +: a new sound), PRESETS the rhythms. 21 sound recipes (7 a voice), 12 rhythm recipes. A REVERB send a voice into SPACE; the dry drums after the reverb. Sessions keep them; older sessions load without touching them. They run on CPU1 with the output stage.
  • The MASTER knob is read before any sound: the splash played for about 1 second at half volume, the knob down or not.
  • tools/fm1_bench.py patches-drums: the load with the drums at their densest.

Build 15 (2026-11-10)

  • HOME and SHIFT + HOME as on Tonitor: HOME a new patch from any recipe, always; SHIFT + HOME a new patch from the recipe named in the main view (the playing patch's, or the one PRESETS turned to). PRESETS turns through the recipes from the one playing. ANY is gone.

Build 14 (2026-11-10)

  • No more silence under the RHYTHM: in the host's test every recipe with every style (400 pairs) now sounds, the quietest at -33 dB (build 13: 6 near silent, down to -58 dB). 3 causes, 3 fixes:
    • A channel in a ring was choked by KICK and CHOKE: the ring died between the hits and never grew back. Now its gate cuts what is heard, and the ring runs on.
    • A sparse lane (a hit or 2 a bar, short) left its channel all but silent: it is chopped now, over a bed 14 dB down.
    • The trim measured a quiet output, chopped by the RHYTHM, as silence, and never brought it up (32 dB short in 1 case). Its measure is finer now.
  • The RHYTHM's test plays every recipe with every style, and fails under -40 dB (before: every 3rd recipe, -50).

Build 13 (2026-11-10)

  • SEQ now reaches the chosen channel's motion: OUT, OUT EQ, OUT FX, then LFO 1, LFO 2, MOD 1 TO 4, MOD 5 TO 8, then back to the channel's page. OCT- / OCT+ step through them there. A channel's own OCT pages end at FX.
  • A new recipe, FREE: no direction, anything goes as long as it sounds (every connection, voice, effect and space as likely as the next, over the widest ranges; its gestures to destinations drawn per channel). On PRESETS it sits last, beside ANY. Tested: 200 FREE patches, none quiet, none clipped.
  • A muted channel is grey too, even while the RHYTHM runs.
  • Known: the RHYTHM's KICK and CHOKE can choke a ring of channels to near silence (6 of 400 recipe x style pairs in the host's test, in several recipes, FREE among them). Not changed yet.

Build 12 (2026-11-10)

  • A gesture loop for each channel, each on its own (as Tonitor's looper is a layer's): REC and PLAY act on the chosen channel; a channel's loop records only that channel (its parameters and its effect slot) and replaces the loop it had (no overdubs). The loops play together, each its own length. Only 1 records at a time: REC on another channel ends the recording and arms that one. Sessions keep each channel's loop; a session saved before, with 1 loop for all, loads as a loop for each channel it touched (the output's and the RHYTHM's changes left out).
  • HOME draws from any recipe until PRESETS chooses one (as on Tonitor). PRESETS has a position for that, ANY, before the first recipe and after the last. SHIFT + HOME: another recipe than the one playing. A session loaded: none chosen.
  • Each start is a new patch, from any recipe, and its tempo is drawn between 91 and 299 BPM (before: always the same DRONE at 120). The randomness comes from the ADCs' noise and the clock at power-on.
  • A channel not in the patch (muted, or its LEVEL and SENDs off with no RHYTHM) is drawn in grey: its number, its name, its meter, its pages; in the OVERVIEW too.

Build 11 (2026-11-10)

  • PRESETS no longer flashes "RECIPE": turning it changes the name in the main view, in place, to the recipe's (from another page it goes to the main view). Before, the flash went and the main view still named the patch playing. HOME draws from the recipe named; turned back to the patch's own recipe, the patch's name is shown again.

Build 10 (2026-11-10)

  • PRESETS are gone: there were 16 fixed "factory patches" and a page of them. The knob now shows the RECIPE (an archetype, never a fixed patch): its name, flashed, and nothing else changes. HOME draws a new patch from the recipe shown, otherwise each time; SHIFT + HOME from another recipe, at random. No page of its own.
  • 8 new recipes, 24 in all: CHOIR, ENGINE, INSECTS, ORGAN, MORSE, FURNACE, AURORA, SONAR. They reach for the effects the first 16 use little (RESONATOR, XMOD, SAG, OCTAVER, REED, DIFFUSER, GATE, CUTS). A session keeps its recipe as before (the first 16 keep their numbers).
  • The RHYTHM's pages: OCT+ / OCT- between TEMPO SWING CHAOS LENGTH and a 2nd page, MIX: how much of the gates is heard against the loops as they run on (100 %: all gate, as before; 0 %: the loops alone). KICK's bursts and ACCENT's pushes follow it. Stored in the rhythm's spare byte: older sessions load at 100 %.
  • GATES is now LENGTH (the gates' length; "GATE LENGTH" does not fit beside its bar).
  • The start: a DRONE (the same patch as before, named after its recipe).

Build 9 (2026-11-10)

  • CPU0 made room: over the same 30 drawn patches (tools/fm1_bench.py), a block's load is 64 % on average (build 8: 76 %, build 7: 91 %), 82 % at worst (build 8: 102 %), and no patch runs late (build 8: 3 did, all 6 channels live). The sound is unchanged: the host's renders are build 8's, bit for bit.
    • Each channel's strip runs inside the sample loop, not called (the call, a channel a sample, cost more than the tube); its input is read through a pointer set once a block; sends and pan worked out only when not 0.
    • The parameters copied each block a halfword at a time, in RAM (the compiler's copy went bytewise, to the flash).
    • USB's 6 channel lanes are made on CPU1 with the output stage, and now line up with the output (before, they came a block ahead of it).
    • The tanh, exp2, log2 and filter tables in RAM, off the flash's cache.
  • tools/fm1_bench.py costs-of I: a drawn patch's costs, a block in parts (copies, modulation, coefficients, gains, samples, the tail), and the CPU's clock (324 MHz).
  • The build stays -Os: built -O2, the update loader never answers (the FM-1 sits in update mode until power-cycled), and the app comes up on USB but never answers there (UBOOT was the way back).

Build 8 (2026-11-10)

  • The screen reader removed, whole: its voice, its words, GLOBAL SETUP's SETTINGS (SCREEN READER, SPEECH RATE) and SHIFT + black key 8. A stored GLOBAL SETUP still loads (its 2 bytes kept, unused). The image 15 KiB smaller.
  • CPU0, measured on the FM-1 (tools/fm1_bench.py): every drawn patch ran at 85 .. 100 % (half of them late), CPU1 at 20 %. The effects are not the cause (most ~3 % of a sample each; RESONATOR 8.6, DIFFUSER 4.8): the 6 channel strips are (~9 % each, run whether heard or not), and the coefficients worked out anew each block (16 %).
    • A channel's coefficients now each anew only when what they are made of moves (the modulation moved 1 value, the whole channel was redone).
    • A channel that reaches nothing (muted, or LEVEL and both SENDs off, no RHYTHM on it) is not run; back, it starts from silence. Its insert, if any, runs on.
    • A shelf or the peak at 0 dB is not run, unless a modulation slot moves it. The sound is unchanged: the host's renders are the same as build 7's, bit for bit.
  • tools/fm1_bench.py: each effect's, each strip's and a block's cost measured on the FM-1, and the load of drawn patches as they play (firmware/src/bench.c, over USB MIDI).

Build 7 (2026-11-10)

  • Fixes builds 5 and 6 coming up without USB (nothing reached the FM-1, not even the installer; UBOOT was the way back). The every-block part of the mixer (the coefficients, the modulation, the rhythm, the screen reader's voice (since removed), ~12 KiB) ran from the flash, through its small cache; as it grew, the render filled CPU0 (~100 %) and USB, served between renders, never started. It runs from RAM now, as Tonitor's renders do. The sound is unchanged, bit for bit.
  • USB can no longer be shut out: if the renders leave it no gap for 2 ms, it is served inside one.
  • The build fails if anything the render calls each block is left in the flash, or the RAM for code runs low.
  • Includes build 6 (the RHYTHM), never installed.

Build 6 (2026-11-10)

  • The RHYTHM, stage 1: a lane a channel (up to 32 steps, 8 step lengths, accents, gate, depth, chance, rolls, mutation), played CHOP, CHOKE, KICK or ACCENT; 16 styles (INDUSTRIAL, POWER NOISE, BROKEN, AKSAK, POLYMETER, POLYRHYTHM, MARCH, HALFTIME, GABBER, ROLLS, CHOP, TRIBAL, TURING, ERRATIC, SPARSE, CLOCKWORK) drawn for the patch as it sounds. The 2nd black key from the right: on and off; SHIFT +: a new rhythm; held: the TEMPO page (10 .. 500 BPM, SWING, CHAOS, GATES; PRESETS through the styles).
  • Kept with snapshots and sessions; a new patch keeps it playing. Sessions saved by builds 4 and 5 load, the rhythm off.

Build 5 (2026-11-10)

  • 6 effects in the rack, none moving pitch: CYCLES (WAVELOSS, SPUTTER, WAVESET), REED (a clarinet's bore, its note a fixed step), OCTAVER (1 or 2 octaves down), DIFFUSER (4 allpasses), SAG (a power supply starving), CUTS (BBCut-style phrases of cuts and rolls; GLITCH unchanged). Their notes, modes, sizes and windows are steps, out of the modulation's reach. The families use them.
  • Sessions saved by build 4 load as they were.

Build 4 (2026-11-10)

  • FOLD in every channel, after the tube: a wavefolder (x 1.2 .. x 16), more harmonics as it is driven, never more level. On the AMP page (TUBE, GAIN, FOLD, OP-AMP; SHIFT: MODE), a modulation destination, in the families.
  • 4 effects in the rack: RESONATOR (6 tuned resonators, a root and a chord, fixed: no modulation reaches its tuning), XMOD (ring, XOR, fold, compare with another channel or bus), DUCK and GATE (keyed by another channel or bus). The families use them.
  • DELAY's and FLANGER's feedback keep their rounding error (after ChoralRoot's FM-1 delay): repeats fade as they should.
  • No pitch shifting or frequency shifting added, on purpose.
  • Build numbers only: the release option gone; each build tagged build-N in git and kept as build/lilliput-build-N.fwsc.
  • Sessions saved by build 3 are not read.

Build 3 (2026-11-10)

  • The modulation on pages of its own, the channel's last: LFO 1, LFO 2, and the matrix — now 8 slots — on MOD 1 TO 4 and MOD 5 TO 8 (KNOB: amount; SHIFT + KNOB: destination; PRESETS: source of the slot in hand).
  • SHIFT + black key 1: the chosen channel, every parameter at random (its mute kept).
  • The GESTURE loop: REC arms, the first change records, REC ends and plays; PLAY plays or stops it; REC held empties it. Every change on any channel. The output's mute moves to SHIFT + PLAY.
  • SNAPSHOTS: SAVE short opens them; 16 whole-mixer states on the white keys (held: store; short: recall; SHIFT: empty), with a morph time (KNOB 1, up to 30 s). Kept with the session, as is the gesture loop.
  • The screen: a 2nd canvas (1 band drawn while the last is sent), the panel's link at 20 MHz (was 12), the main view drawn without a wipe — pages change about twice as fast.
  • Sessions saved by build 2 are not read.

Build 2 (2026-11-10)

  • LEVEL: 1 dB a detent up to -5 dB, then 0.1 dB a detent; PAN: 1 step a detent, L 50 .. R 50.
  • 16 families of patches, as Tonitor's: each its connections, its voicing, its effects, its space and its motion. HOME: another family; SHIFT + HOME: the same family; SHIFT + PRESETS: the family before or after; HOME held: the nudge.
  • Tonitor's LFOs and modulation matrix on every channel: the MOD page (after FX), SHIFT + SEQ for a random one; sources LFO 1 and 2, the channel's own loudness, the output's, a random value at each onset.
  • The pages redrawn: names small, values large on their own line, nothing over anything; SHIFT held shows a page's switches; text sized to fit, never squeezed. A test checks every word fits.
  • The trim keeps the peaks under -4 dB, and a guard brings the main level down if the output holds at its ceiling.
  • Sessions saved by build 1 are not read.

Build 1 (2026-11-10)

The first build of Lilliput: a no-input mixer for the M-VAVE FM-1, after NoInputMixer, on Tonitor's screen and platform (Tonitor build 74), with none of Tonitor's engines.

  • 6 channels a sample at a time: input selector (PRE, POST, MIX L/R, SEND 1/2, RET 1/2, NONE, CH 1-6), noise generator (6 types), preamp, 6 tubes, 6 op-amps, overload protection, shelves or cuts, peak, notch or band-pass, brickwall limiter, 2 sends, level, pan, main mix.
  • A rack of 7 slots: DELAY, FLANGER, CHORUS, TREMOLO, FORMANT, BITCRUSH, GLITCH.
  • The output: returns, equaliser, insert, SPACE (6 reverb spaces), main level; on CPU1.
  • HOME draws a new patch from 6 recipes; SHIFT + HOME nudges it; each patch woken up and trimmed to a single loudness.
  • 16 factory patches, 64 sessions (their own record: other firmwares' data left alone), GLOBAL SETUP, MIDI CCs, USB audio of the output or the 6 channels, the screen reader.
